title: Rwanda Family Gorilla Trekking When Not Everyone Is Old Enough to Go
meta_title: Family Gorilla Trekking in Rwanda With Under-15s
meta_description: Family gorilla trekking in Rwanda: the age-15 rule, what younger kids do instead, permit fees and how two or three families share one safari.
excerpt: Family gorilla trekking in Rwanda is open only to those aged 15 or over, so the best family trips plan a split day. Here is who treks, what younger children do instead, and how groups of families share vehicles and rooms.
content:
Family gorilla trekking in Rwanda works only for members aged 15 or over: the Rwanda Development Board will not issue a gorilla permit to anyone younger. Families with younger children still go, but they plan a split day, with the under-15s doing golden monkeys, a conservation campus or a village visit instead.

That age rule is the first thing most parents trip over when planning family gorilla trekking. This guide covers who can trek, what everyone else does, what it costs, and how a group of two or three families shares vehicles and rooms. If you would rather hand the logistics over, our family safari planning team builds this kind of trip every week from Nairobi.

Quick Facts

  • Gorilla trekking age: 15 years minimum, set by the Rwanda Development Board
  • Gorilla permit: USD 1,500 per foreign non-resident (checked November 2026)
  • Golden monkey trekking: From age 12, USD 100 per foreigner (checked November 2026)
  • Group size: Maximum 8 visitors per gorilla family, one hour with them
  • Kigali to Volcanoes National Park: About 2.5 hours by road
  • Best for younger kids: Akagera game drives and boat trips, the Ellen DeGeneres Campus, Lake Kivu

What Is the Minimum Age for Family Gorilla Trekking in Rwanda?

The minimum age for family gorilla trekking in Rwanda is 15 years, with no exceptions for tall or sporty children. The rule is published on the Rwanda Development Board's own booking portal and applies to every gorilla family in Volcanoes National Park.

You can read the official conditions on the Rwanda Development Board gorilla tracking page. It lists the permit at USD 1,500 for foreign non-residents, a maximum of eight visitors per group, registration at 07:00 at the park offices in Kinigi, one hour with the gorillas and a seven-metre distance (all checked November 2026). Fees change, so confirm before you book.

Why the age limit exists

Mountain gorillas catch human illnesses easily, and children pick up colds more often than adults. The trek can also be hard: some gorilla families live high on the Virunga slopes, with steep, wet ground and nettles. A frightened child who runs or shouts near a silverback is a risk nobody wants, which is why family gorilla trekking stops at 15.

Family gorilla trekking with a mixed-age group

Book permits only for those who will be 15 on the trekking date, and carry everyone's passport on the day. A 14-year-old with a birthday the week after the trek cannot go. Anyone with a cold or flu is also asked not to trek, so build in a spare day if your teenagers are prone to catching something on the flight. Our guide to how hard gorilla trekking really is explains the fitness side in more detail.

How Do Families Split the Gorilla Trekking Day?

On family gorilla trekking trips, most groups split the day in two: the over-15s leave the lodge around 06:00 for the Kinigi briefing, while younger children sleep in and do a shorter outing with one parent. Everyone meets again for lunch, and the trekkers usually return by early afternoon.

The trick in family gorilla trekking is deciding early which adult stays behind. In a group of two or three families, parents can take turns over two trekking days, so every adult gets a turn and no child is left with a stranger. That needs two permit dates, so book months ahead.

What can under-15s do near Volcanoes National Park?

The area around Musanze has more for children than parents expect. Good half-day choices on a family gorilla trekking day include:

  • The Ellen DeGeneres Campus of the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund near the park entrance, with a conservation gallery, films and a recreation of Dian Fossey's cabin. Allow one to two hours.
  • The Gorilla Guardians Village, where families can watch traditional dancing and drumming.
  • Golden monkey trekking for anyone aged 12 to 14, in the bamboo zone of the same park.

Golden monkey trekking is the best family gorilla trekking substitute for a 12- to 14-year-old, with the same rangers and forest. Our post on golden monkey trekking in Rwanda covers what the walk is like.

Which Rwanda Activities Suit Each Age?

Rwanda's age limits are clear once you see them side by side: gorillas, chimpanzees and the Dian Fossey tomb hike start at 15, golden monkeys at 12, and Akagera game drives and boat trips have no published minimum age. Children aged 5 and under enter Akagera and Nyungwe free.

Akagera: The Safari Part Every Age Can Share

Akagera National Park is where the whole family, toddlers included, gets a proper Big Five safari. It lies about 110 km east of Kigali, roughly two and a half to three hours by road, so it fits neatly at the start or end of a Rwanda trip.

Game drives here are relaxed, with lakes, giraffe plains and open savannah in the north. The scheduled boat trip on Lake Ihema is a highlight for children: hippos, crocodiles and water birds at close range, with no walking at all. Akagera's 2025 price list also shows a private boat at a flat rate per boat, which suits two families travelling together and avoids sharing a boat with strangers.

Because Akagera is where everybody does everything together, we usually put it before the family gorilla trekking days. Children who have already seen lions and elephants mind less about missing the gorillas. If you are comparing countries, our Uganda family safari guide shows how the same split-day approach works in Bwindi.

Is Nyungwe Worth Adding for Teenagers?

Nyungwe is worth adding if you have teenagers of 15 or over who want chimpanzees, and time for a long drive. The park is about five to six hours from Kigali, so it needs at least two nights to justify the journey.

Chimpanzee tracking in Nyungwe follows the same 15-plus rule as gorillas, and starts very early because chimps move fast once they wake. The canopy walkway is the activity the whole family can share: a suspended walkway above the forest, guided, with a minimum of two and a maximum of eight guests per departure on the park's price sheet. Nyungwe's price sheet does not publish a minimum age for the walkway, so ask when booking if you have very young children.

Families with only under-12s often skip Nyungwe for Lake Kivu: fewer hours in the car and more time by the water before the flight home.

How Much Does Family Gorilla Trekking Cost for a Group?

For a group, the cost of family gorilla trekking is driven first by permits: USD 1,500 for each person aged 15 or over (checked November 2026), and nothing for younger children because they cannot trek. Everything else, from vehicles to rooms, depends on how many families travel and how they want to share.

Vehicles and rooms for two or three families

Two families of four normally need two vehicles, which suits family gorilla trekking well: one vehicle leaves early for the briefing while the other waits for the younger children. Families with children close in age sometimes share one vehicle on Akagera days and split on the trekking day.

For rooms, ask for family or interconnecting rooms, which lodges near Volcanoes offer in limited numbers and which fill early in the dry months of June to September.

On our 6 day Rwanda family safari, every seventh place is free for each six paying travellers, each family can pay separately, and people can arrive on different flights. A deposit of 30 to 40 percent holds the booking, with the balance due two to four weeks before travel. Group quotes are priced individually, because dates, ages and rooming change everything.

A Seven-Day Rwanda Family Gorilla Trekking Plan

Seven days is the sweet spot for Rwanda family gorilla trekking: enough for Akagera, a calm gorilla day and a lake finish. The plan below adds a gorilla trek and an extra night near the park to our six-day family route.

DayPlanWho does what
1Arrive in Kigali, rest at the hotelEveryone
2Drive to Akagera, sunset boat trip on Lake IhemaEveryone
3Full-day Akagera game drive, return to KigaliEveryone
4Kigali city tour, drive to Musanze, Ellen DeGeneres CampusEveryone
5Gorilla trekking dayOver-15s trek; 12-14s do golden monkeys; younger children visit the Gorilla Guardians Village with a parent
6Drive to Lake Kivu, afternoon by the waterEveryone
7Boat trip on Lake Kivu, return to Kigali for flightsEveryone

Want both parents to go family gorilla trekking? Add a second gorilla day on day 6 and move Lake Kivu by a day. The 2 day gorilla and golden monkey trek shows how a short Volcanoes stay runs if you are bolting this onto a longer East Africa trip.

Insider Tips for Family Groups

  • Book permits first: For family gorilla trekking, secure gorilla dates for every over-15 before flights or lodges
  • Check birthdays: A child who turns 15 a week after the trek cannot go; count the trekking date
  • Hire a porter: Porters carry bags and give a steadying hand on steep ground, which helps nervous teens
  • Pack for mud: Long trousers, gardening gloves for nettles and waterproof boots; see our packing list
  • Stay two nights near the park: Avoid a 04:00 departure from Kigali on the trekking day
  • Keep a spare day: If a teenager has a cold, the rangers will ask them not to trek

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a 12-year-old go gorilla trekking in Rwanda?

No. A 12-year-old cannot join family gorilla trekking in Rwanda, because the Rwanda Development Board sets the minimum age at 15. A 12-year-old can do golden monkey trekking, which starts at age 12, plus the Ellen DeGeneres Campus, Akagera game drives and boat trips.

How much does family gorilla trekking in Rwanda cost per person?

The gorilla permit alone is USD 1,500 per foreign non-resident aged 15 or over (checked November 2026), and younger children do not need one because they cannot trek. Lodging, a private vehicle, a guide and park fees for other activities come on top, so most families budget the permits first and build the rest of the trip around them.

What do younger children do while the family treks gorillas?

On the trekking day, younger children usually stay at the lodge with one parent or a trusted adult, then spend a gentle morning at the Ellen DeGeneres Campus or the Gorilla Guardians Village near Musanze. Family gorilla trekking groups with grandparents often split the day this way and meet again for lunch.

Is gorilla trekking safe for teenagers?

Yes, for a reasonably fit teenager of 15 or over, gorilla trekking in Rwanda is safe when they follow the rangers. Groups are capped at eight visitors per gorilla family, armed rangers and trackers lead every walk, and the visit lasts one hour at a distance of about seven metres. The main challenges are steep, muddy slopes and altitude, not the gorillas.

How many days does a Rwanda family safari with gorillas need?

Six to seven days suits most families. That allows a night in Kigali on arrival, a night or two in Akagera for the Big Five, two nights near Volcanoes National Park so the trekking day is not rushed, and a final night on Lake Kivu. Add two more days if the teenagers also want chimpanzees in Nyungwe.

Final Thoughts

Family gorilla trekking in Rwanda means planning around one firm rule: only those aged 15 or over meet the gorillas. The best trips give everyone else something just as memorable, from Akagera's lions to golden monkeys and Lake Kivu, so the youngest traveller never feels left out.
